body.text: Travelling home to the UK, US or Europe after a procedure in Istanbul is mostly a logistics exercise once you leave the clinic. [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about) is an independent, client-paid, flat-fee advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
How do sleeping position, washing and scab removal work from Day 1 to Day 10?

From Day 1 to Day 10, clinics typically advise sleeping semi-upright to limit forehead swelling, keeping hands off the recipient area and following a written gentle-wash protocol until crusts soften and shed naturally. Because protocols vary by surgeon, always follow your clinic's discharge sheet rather than generic online timelines.

Swelling peaks early and crusts form over tiny incisions within days. Per [NHS hair transplant recovery guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/hair-transplant/), grafts are not yet secure during the first two weeks, bandages usually come off after 2 to 5 days without touching grafts, and gentle hand washing often begins around Day 6. The [International Society of Hair Restoration Surgery (ISHRS)](https://ishrs.org/after-hair-restoration-surgery/) also emphasizes following your surgeon's exact post-operative routine.

body.text: When can you wear a loose hat, return to office work or exercise?

Most desk-based travellers plan 7 to 14 days away from in-person office work, wait for explicit surgeon sign-off before wearing a loose, breathable hat and pause strenuous exercise for at least two to four weeks. Tight caps, helmets, heavy sweating and direct sun exposure can irritate healing skin or dislodge early grafts.

Your exact timeline depends on your job and surgical method. [NHS recovery guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/hair-transplant/) notes that patients often need 1 to 2 weeks off work and may need to cut back on exercise during the first month to reduce scarring risk. Remote workers often resume laptop work after 3 to 5 days, while physical roles require longer rest. Still comparing clinics? Read our [questions to ask before booking a hair transplant in Istanbul](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/hair-transplant-checklist-istanbul).
What items must go in checked luggage vs carry-on (liquids over 100ml)?

Any clinic-supplied shampoo, foam, lotion or saline bottle larger than 100ml (3.4 oz) must go in checked luggage unless it qualifies as an essential liquid medicine with written documentation. Packing a checked bag for your return flight prevents airport security from confiscating your post-op wash kit at Istanbul Airport.

Both [UK GOV hand luggage liquid rules](https://www.gov.uk/hand-luggage-restrictions/liquids) and the [TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule](https://www.tsa.gov/travel/frequently-asked-questions/liquids-aerosols-and-gels-rule) restrict carry-on liquids, gels and aerosols to 100ml (3.4 oz) containers. While [UK GOV essential medicines guidance](https://www.gov.uk/hand-luggage-restrictions/essential-medicines-and-medical-equipment) and [TSA medical screening rules](https://www.tsa.gov/travel/security-screening/whatcanibring/medical) permit medically necessary liquids over 100ml when declared, cosmetic washes are frequently stopped. Checking a suitcase avoids that risk.

items: Checked luggage: Clinic foam cleanser, post-op shampoo over 100ml, large saline bottles and recovery lotions in leak-proof zip bags.
Carry-on bag: Prescribed oral medications in original labelled boxes, printed discharge summary, U-shaped neck pillow and one under-100ml saline mist if cleared.
Travel-day clothing: Button-up or zip-front shirt so nothing pulls over your scalp during security checks or boarding.
Airport buffer: Book aisle seating and allow extra transfer time so you never bump your head on overhead bins.

body.text: How do you send clear progress photos to your clinic from abroad?

Take your follow-up photos in even, indirect daylight against a plain background from five consistent angles—front hairline, left temple, right temple, crown and donor back—without flash or filters. Consistent lighting and framing let your medical team assess healing accurately and spot irritation early.

Set reminders for Day 3, Day 7, Day 10 and Day 14, or follow your clinic's check-in dates. Ask someone to shoot the crown and donor area at arm's length so the camera focuses cleanly. Contact your clinic promptly if you notice unexpected warmth, throbbing pain or fever. If you want neutral, flat-fee help organizing hotel proximity, private airport transfers and clinic check-in timing in Istanbul without broker commissions, reach out to [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism). faq.q: How long should I stay in Istanbul before flying home?
faq.a: Most travellers stay 2 to 3 nights after the procedure so the clinic can complete the initial check and first demonstration wash. Your surgeon confirms when you are fit to fly.

faq.q: Can I sleep flat on my side after Day 5?
faq.a: Many clinics transition patients off semi-upright sleeping after 3 to 5 days, while others prefer a full week. Follow your surgeon's written discharge schedule.

faq.q: Is shock loss or shedding normal in the first 14 days?
faq.a: Shedding of transplanted hair shafts typically begins after the first couple of weeks before new growth appears around month four, per [NHS guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/hair-transplant/).

faq.q: What if my checked luggage with the wash kit is delayed?
faq.a: Keep your written product list in your carry-on and contact your clinic before buying any substitute pharmacy shampoo or spray.

faq.q: Can I wear a baseball cap at the airport?
faq.a: Avoid tight caps unless your clinic explicitly approves a loose fisherman-style hat that never touches grafted zones.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye provide medical aftercare once I am home?
faq.a: No. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions and handles all medical follow-up questions.
